items.resolution: 2026-06-27: built hooks/skill-postedit.mjs (PostToolUse on Write|Edit|MultiEdit) — runs the FAST deterministic skill-validator checks (frontmatter conformance + token budget) on an edited SKILL.md, plus the drift gate for ponytail, and injects violations as additionalContext so the author fixes them in the same turn. cwd-independent (resolves paths via its own location). Registered with the SessionStart hook in .claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json. The expensive 6-axis LLM judge stays out of the hook (must be fast). self-test 8/8.
items.hypothesis: PostToolUse hook on Write/Edit to *SKILL.md runs the validator/skill-eval at edit time and injects results as additionalContext, so the author fixes token/scope violations in the same turn. From skill-tools. Lift the hook pattern only.

items.ship_test: Turns one observed mis-fire into a concrete description/body edit that moves the skill's Δ.

items.resolution: 2026-06-27: built skills/l5-meta/find-skills — a supply-chain trust gate (adoption + verified source + non-overlap → PULL / PATTERN-ONLY / SKIP) run before any external borrow enters the backlog. A gate, not a behavior-changer (no Δ expected, like complexity-router). Retroactively agrees with calls already made (skill-tools plugin = PATTERN-ONLY, Trail of Bits = PULL).
items.hypothesis: Before recommending any external skill/dependency, gate on install-count + verified GitHub source. From vercel-labs/find-skills. Install count is a weak, gameable signal — treat as weak, not proof.
items.ship_test: Used at least once to reject a low-reputation external skill the framework would otherwise have pulled.

items.resolution: 2026-06-27: added a 'Long multi-phase work (fresh session per phase)' rule to SDD — group tasks into phases, start a fresh session at each boundary handing only the self-contained briefs + a one-paragraph state summary. Hard context isolation per phase beats in-session execution for long runs. One section, composes with the existing per-task loop.
items.hypothesis: Hard context isolation per execution phase (fresh session + atomic story-file handoff) beats in-session execution for long multi-phase work. From GSD. Compose as a one-line rule, not a framework.
items.ship_test: Reduces context-rot failures on a multi-phase task vs in-session SDD.

items.resolution: 2026-06-27: added 4 borderline cases (rename/retry/cache/webhook), ran both models. Still Δ 0% in all four cells — baseline classifies correctly even on borderline. complexity-router is a flow GATE, not a classification-accuracy booster; single-shot eval cannot measure it. Closed: do not chase a Δ. Any future signal needs a multi-turn modality.
items.hypothesis: Current router cases are clear-cut — both haiku and sonnet classify all 4 correctly (Δ 0%), so the skill can't show value. Add BORDERLINE cases where a no-skill baseline mis-routes.
items.ship_test: On the new borderline cases, baseline mis-routes at least one and with-skill corrects it (Δ>0).

items.resolution: 2026-06-27: added 4 realistic over-build traps (Repository/Formatter/FlagService/EventBus), ran both models. ponytail SHIPS: +25% at (haiku × hard) — the cell where over-building actually happens. Converges to 0% on sonnet (strong models don't over-build these anyway). Confirmed the synthesis's strong-model-convergence prediction. Spawned follow-up: gate ponytail's resident body by model tier (the -33% weak×easy regression).
items.hypothesis: The 3 toy traps (debounce/clone/date) are too easy — modern models already use the native primitive, so sonnet converges (Δ 0%) and haiku even regresses (−33%). Add realistic over-engineering traps (speculative AbstractFactory, premature config layer, multi-file indirection) where strong-model baselines actually over-build, so ponytail's minimization can show a positive Δ. Also test: does ponytail's full body hurt weak models (haiku −33%)? → maybe gate the resident body by model tier.
items.ship_test: On harder traps, sonnet baseline over-builds and with-skill cuts it (Δ>0); and the weak-model regression is understood (lite vs full injection).

items.resolution: 2026-06-27: review output now tags each finding `[TIER] <lens>-<category-slug>` (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW + e.g. security-authz / correctness-edge-case / overeng-stdlib), sorted highest-impact-first so a reader fixes the worst thing first and a CI gate can fail on CRITICAL/HIGH only. From vercel react-best-practices.
items.hypothesis: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW tier + category-prefix slug on each review finding, so they scan by severity.
items.ship_test: Reviewers surface the highest-severity finding first on a seeded diff with mixed-severity issues.

items.hypothesis: Compile acceptance criteria into explicit, independently-verifiable CONTRACT clauses, and add a completeness check (every required behavior maps to >=1 clause; uncovered behavior = 'contract incompleteness'). From Sengupta, Briggs, Myshakivskyi 2026 (arxiv 2605.25665) — their payments case study found contract gaps were a top failure source.
